props.title: New Delhi Times

sections.content: **New Delhi Times (1985)** (1985) marked a watershed moment in Indian political cinema, delivering a stark examination of media corruption and political violence through the eyes of an honest newspaper editor. Director Ramesh Sharma crafted a prescient thriller that shares DNA with later media exposés like **Spotlight** (2015) and **The Post** (2017). The film's unflinching look at journalism's moral compromises anticipated contemporary Indian works like **Peepli Live** (2010) and **No One Killed Jessica** (2011), while its style echoes the gritty realism of parallel cinema pioneers like Ardh Satya (1983).

sections.content: The 1980s marked a crucial period for Indian political cinema, with films daring to confront institutional corruption head-on. **New Delhi Times** (1985) stands alongside **Aghaat** (1985) and **Party** (1984) as examples of how filmmakers used thriller frameworks to deliver social commentary. Shashi Kapoor's nuanced performance as editor Vikas Pande set a template for later portrayals of principled journalists, seen in films like **Page 3** (2005) and **Shanghai** (2012).

The film's exploration of media manipulation and political violence remains disturbingly relevant. Its influence can be traced through later works like **Rann** (2010) and **Nayak: The Real Hero** (2001), though few match its documentary-like authenticity. The cinematography by Subrata Mitra, who also shot Satyajit Ray's Apu Trilogy, brings a neo-realist edge that influenced later political thrillers like **Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi** (2003). sections.content: The film's legacy extends beyond its immediate era, influencing contemporary filmmakers tackling institutional corruption. Recent works like **Madaari** (2016) and **Mukkabaaz** (2017) echo its blend of personal story and political critique. The film's National Film Award for Best Film on Social Issues validated a new approach to political storytelling that continues in works like **Article 15** (2019) and **Mulk** (2018).
